newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain government keen for labour deal this week.
newsitem.headline: Spain government keen for labour deal this week.

text.p: Spain's Labour Minister Javier Arenas said on Wednesday he hoped unions and employers would reach an accord on labour reforms this week.
"The government wants an agreement to be reached this week, and if it is today all the better," Arenas said before entering Congress.
"But we must respect the independence of both sides and the great effort and maturity that the unions and employers are showing."
Unions and employers returned to the negotiating table on Wednesday after a five-day break to discuss a fresh proposal from unions.
Unions are bending to employer demands for cheaper dismissal costs in exchange for a more permanent contract.
"The positions of both sides are getting closer on a more effective way to integrate youths into the labour market and on more stable jobs," said Arenas.

But General Workers' Union (UGT) spokesman Manuel Bonmati told a news conference in Santander that a final deal was "being complicated" by the fact that employers "were refusing to budge their position".
The government has given unions and employers until early March to reach a deal before it steps in and imposes it own measures.
